title: Lexicographically Smallest Equivalent String
summary: Given two strings, s1 and s2, of the same length, and another string baseStr, you are to determine the lexicographically smallest string that is equivalent to baseStr.
statement: Given two strings, s1 and s2, of the same length, and another string baseStr, you are to determine the lexicographically smallest string that is equivalent to baseStr. Two characters are considered equivalent if they are the same or if they are related through a series of equivalences defined by the characters in s1 and s2. These equivalences follow the rules of reflexivity (a == a), symmetry (if a == b then b == a), and transitivity (if a == b and b == c then a == c). The resulting equivalent string should be the lexicographically smallest among all possible equivalent strings.
constraints: Replace each base character with the smallest letter in its component.
hints: Union equivalent letters while retaining the smallest root.
For each pair attach the larger root to the smaller; translate base characters through find.
Transitive closure is captured by components and the root invariant gives the lexicographically smallest replacement.
editorial: Transitive closure is captured by components and the root invariant gives the lexicographically smallest replacement.
